channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Chinese Scientists Establish Satellite Communication Link Between Arctic and Antarctic
item.description: Chinese scientists have successfully established a satellite communication link between the Arctic and Antarctic using the Guowang satellite system. The connection was made from ships in the Arctic to China's "Qinling" station in Antarctica, with data transmission speeds reaching 30 Mbps and latency under one second.

item.title: Afghan Educator Donates $2.5 Million to Oxford for Afghan Women's Scholarships
item.description: Shabana Basij-Rasikh, founder of the School of Leadership, Afghanistan, has donated $2.5 million to establish a permanent scholarship at the University of Oxford for Afghan women. The scholarship will cover full tuition, living expenses, and include leadership training, aiming to provide educational access for women facing educational barriers.

item.title: Astana Resident Scams Five Individuals Under Guise of Marketplace Investments
item.description: A resident of Astana has been sentenced to six years in prison for defrauding five people. She offered online marketplace training, then convinced victims to invest money for goods, promising returns. The funds were misused, causing a total loss of 15.6 million tenge.

item.title: Flydubai Co-Pilot Planned 9/11-Style Attack on Tel Aviv, Prosecutors Say
item.description: A Flydubai co-pilot, identified as Hammam Al-Hammami from Oman, confessed to planning a suicide attack inspired by 9/11. He intended to crash a Boeing 737 Max into Ben Gurion Airport. The suspect had made reconnaissance flights and passed security checks before the attempted hijacking.

item.title: Kazakhstan Awarded Hosting Rights for 2027 World Judo Championships
item.description: Kazakhstan has been awarded the hosting rights for the 2027 World Judo Championships, with the event to be held in Astana. The flag handover ceremony took place in Baku during the current championships. This event is a significant qualifier for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

item.title: UN Report Details Devastating Consequences for Children in Afghanistan Due to Insecurity and Restrictions
item.description: A UN report by Secretary-General António Guterres highlights the devastating impact of insecurity, poverty, displacement, and explosive ordnance on children in Afghanistan. Increased border clashes with Pakistan have further affected them. Between 2023-2025, 4,582 grave violations against children were verified, with 1,415 killed or injured, 80% by explosive ordnance. The Taliban were attributed the largest number of violations.

item.title: Rethinking Afghanistan's Political Culture: Beyond War and Intervention
item.description: Afghanistan's persistent political failures stem from ingrained cultural norms and habits, not just war and foreign intervention. Despite vast resources for nation-building and a new constitution, the republic collapsed in 2021. Personality-driven politics, religious justifications for power, and a lack of principles have repeatedly led to crises and regime failures.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Social Health Insurance Fund Saves 23.4 Billion Tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Finance reports that transferring the Social Health Insurance Fund (SHIF) under its purview has prevented financial losses and restructured the system. An AI-based anti-fraud system helped save 23.4 billion tenge, with efforts underway to recover over 7.9 billion tenge in illegally paid funds. Savings are directed to healthcare financing.

item.title: Kyrgyz Journalist Honored with International Award for Opposition Reporting
item.description: An opposition journalist from Kyrgyzstan has been awarded an international prize for their work. The recognition highlights the journalist's contributions to independent reporting and their role in shedding light on critical issues within the country.

item.title: Kazakhstan Citizen Recovers Lost $10,000 in Tashkent Metro Thanks to Face ID Technology
item.description: A citizen of Kazakhstan accidentally dropped $10,000 (4.5 million tenge) in the Tashkent metro but was unaware of the loss until reaching the car market. A fellow passenger found the money and handed it to metro security. Uzbekistan's Interior Ministry used Face ID technology to identify and return the full amount to the owner.

item.title: Investigative Journalist Bolot Temirov Receives International 'The Albies' Award in London
item.description: Investigative journalist Bolot Temirov, whose materials were declared 'extremist' in Kyrgyzstan, has received the international 'The Albies' award from the 'For Justice' foundation. The award ceremony took place in London. The award recognizes the international recognition of Temirov's projects, Temirov Live and 'Ait, Ait Dese'.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prevents 23.4 Billion Tenge Losses After Social Health Fund Transfer to Finance Ministry
item.description: Kazakhstan has prevented financial losses of 23.4 billion tenge following the transfer of the Social Health Insurance Fund to the Ministry of Finance. The ministry reported that channels of funding leakage were identified and closed, with over 7.9 billion tenge illegally paid to providers being recovered through criminal cases. These recovered funds are being directed towards medical care payments.

item.title: Book on Islam Karimov's Main Opponent Presented in Istanbul and Samarkand
item.description: A two-volume biographical book, "The Man Who Woke Up Early," about Uzbek poet, dissident, and politician Muhammad Salih, the founder of the "Erk" opposition party, was presented in Istanbul. The book, authored by Karimberdi Turamurod, covers Salih's life in Uzbekistan until 1993 and his life in exile from then until the present. A presentation also took place in Samarkand.

item.title: Taliban Rule in Afghanistan Challenges Nation-State Relationship and Citizen Rights
item.description: The Taliban's rule in Afghanistan, established without popular will or free political choice, challenges the fundamental "nation-state" relationship. This relationship, based on consent and accountability, is undermined by the Taliban's reliance on force, coercion, and decree-based governance. The group lacks clear political, legal, and constitutional responsibility towards the people, jeopardizing citizens' rights and government legitimacy.

item.title: Kabul Residents Complain About Soaring LPG Prices and Lack of Market Oversight
item.description: Kabul residents are protesting rising liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices and inconsistent rates across the city, citing increased living costs. Despite official price lists, gas is sold at varying prices without effective monitoring. Residents suggest boosting domestic production to reduce import dependency and mitigate global market impacts on fuel costs.

item.title: US State Department Places Afghanistan in Tier 3 of Human Trafficking Report
item.description: The US Department of State has classified Afghanistan as Tier 3 in its 2026 Trafficking in Persons Report. This designation is due to concerns regarding forced labor, child exploitation, and insufficient protection for trafficking victims. The report indicates Afghanistan has not met minimum standards for combating human trafficking and has not made significant efforts to improve the situation.

item.title: Ghor Province Residents Accuse Taliban of Corruption, Coercion, and Land Grabbing
item.description: Residents of Firozkoh, Ghor Province, have accused local Taliban officials of corruption, coercion, and extortion, stating there is no recourse for complaints. They allege that over five years, the Taliban have violated rights, seized land, and suppressed dissent out of fear. Residents also claim state property has been looted and funds collected for road construction may have been embezzled.

item.title: UN Rapporteur Urges Lifting US Sanctions on ICC, Continuation of Afghanistan Investigation
item.description: Richard Bennett, UN Special Rapporteur on human rights in Afghanistan, called for the immediate lifting of US sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC). He stressed the importance of the ICC continuing its investigation into the situation in Afghanistan, expressing confidence that US sanctions would not hinder progress. Bennett's remarks align with the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights' condemnation of the sanctions.

item.title: Central Asian Summit Advances Regional Cooperation and International Standing
item.description: The consultative summit in Avaza marks a new phase of regional cooperation, strengthening Central Asia's international position. Key goals include deepening collaboration in trade, transport, energy, and technology. Uzbekistan proposed an international conference in Tashkent to foster dialogue on peace and connectivity, emphasizing increased trade and joint production.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans Six-Month Ban on White Sugar Imports
item.description: Kyrgyzstan intends to prohibit the import of white sugar for a period of six months. This measure aims to regulate the domestic sugar market. The specific reasons and details of the ban are expected to be announced soon.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Canada Strengthen Cooperation in Geology and Resource Exploration
item.description: Uzbekistan and Canada are enhancing collaboration in geology, focusing on advanced technologies for seismic data processing and subsurface visualization. A meeting between Uzbekistan's Ministry of Mining and Geology and Canada's Thrust Belt Imaging (TBI) discussed potential partnerships in geophysics, exploration, and energy sectors.

item.title: OSCE Media Forum on Information Accuracy and Trust in Media Held in Bishkek
item.description: An OSCE media forum on information accuracy and trust in media for Central Asia took place in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. Organized by the OSCE Representative on Freedom of the Media, the event focused on strengthening cooperation and dialogue regarding media freedom, journalistic ethics, and ensuring information accuracy to build societal trust.

item.title: Uzbekistan Participates in Inter-Parliamentary Union Health Committee Meetings
item.description: A delegation from Uzbekistan attended meetings of the Inter-Parliamentary Union's Health Committee and a seminar on mental health during the 153rd Assembly. Discussions focused on reproductive health, maternal and child protection, and strengthening legislative frameworks and budget financing. International organizations participated in a dialogue on women's health and adolescent reproductive health.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Role in the CIS: 35 Years On and Future Prospects
item.description: As the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) approaches its 35th anniversary, Uzbekistan has significantly intensified its engagement since 2017, participating in all 66 areas of activity and proposing 90 initiatives, 80 of which are implemented. Uzbekistan will chair the organization in 2027, aiming to address existing challenges and tasks.

item.title: Kokshetau to Receive Natural Gas Within Three Years Via New Pipeline
item.description: Kokshetau and six districts in the Akmola region will be supplied with natural gas within three years through the 'Ishim – Astana' main pipeline. This project, extending the 'Saryarka' gas transmission system, aims to provide access to over 120,000 subscribers, potentially reaching 480,000 users.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans Mandatory Digital Marking for Vegetable Oil by July 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan is proposing to introduce mandatory digital marking for vegetable oil starting July 1, 2027. A draft government resolution, open for discussion until October 24, aims to prevent illegal import, production, and sale of the product. This initiative follows similar digital marking systems implemented for tobacco, alcohol, medicines, and beverages.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks First in Central Asia in Most Powerful Countries Index
item.description: Kazakhstan has entered the top 100 most powerful countries globally, securing 34th place in an international ranking based on U.S. News & World Report research. The nation leads Central Asia, surpassing several neighbors. The ranking assesses economic and political influence, leadership, international partnerships, and military alliances.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Social Health Insurance System Prevents 234 Billion Tenge Losses
item.description: Kazakhstan's mandatory social health insurance system has prevented financial losses amounting to 234 billion tenge over nine months, according to the Ministry of Finance. Efforts to strengthen control have also led to the recovery of over 79 billion tenge illegally paid to medical service providers. New tools, including AI-based anti-fraud measures, are being used to prevent unjustified payments and ensure funds are used for medical care.

item.title: Mass Detentions of Protesters in India: Police Block New Delhi and Restrict Internet
item.description: Thousands were detained in India's capital during protests against electoral roll revisions. Police blocked access to the protest site, restricted public transport, and limited mobile internet. Opposition politicians and activists were among those detained, with demands for the chief election commissioner's resignation.

item.title: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas Postpones Parliamentary and Presidential Elections to 2027
item.description: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas has issued a decree postponing both the parliamentary and presidential elections, now scheduled to take place simultaneously on September 11, 2027. The parliamentary elections were previously set for November 28 of this year, while presidential elections were expected in early 2027. Abbas has been in power for over two decades.

item.title: Uzbekistan Expands Cooperation in Standardization with International Partners
item.description: Uzbekistan participated in the 20th plenary session of ISO/TC 100 in China, alongside delegations from France, Germany, and the UK. Discussions focused on international standardization, chain drive technologies, sustainable development, and greenhouse gas emissions reporting.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks 34th in Most Powerful Countries 2026 Index, Surpassing Several European and Middle Eastern Nations
item.description: Kazakhstan secured the 34th position in the Most Powerful Countries 2026 ranking by World Population Review, based on U.S. News & World Report data. The index assesses countries on economic and political influence, leadership, and alliances. Kazakhstan ranked higher than Denmark, UAE, and Norway, with China, the US, and India leading the list.

item.title: 17-Year-Old Uzbek Citizen Subjected to Violence in Turkey Repatriated Home
item.description: A 17-year-old Uzbek citizen, who was taken to Turkey under the guise of education, faced forced marriage, physical violence, and forced labor. The minor has been repatriated to Uzbekistan following intervention. The case highlights concerns about exploitation of young individuals abroad.

item.title: Kazakhstan Expands Access to Mental Health Services in Polyclinics
item.description: Kazakhstan is enhancing mental healthcare accessibility by integrating services into polyclinics, with 304 primary mental health centers and offices operating nationwide. Over 874,000 outpatient visits were recorded in the first half of 2026. The country focuses on early detection, outpatient treatment, and rehabilitation, increasing daytime psychiatric beds and support for children.

item.title: New bridge under construction and airport modernization underway in Kazakhstan's Pavlodar region
item.description: Kazakhstan's Pavlodar region is developing its transport infrastructure with a new bridge over the Irtysh River and modernization of the Pavlodar Airport. The bridge, featuring an extradosed design, is 690 meters long. Airport upgrades include runway refurbishment and planned terminal expansion to boost air traffic, including international routes.

item.title: Afghan UN Envoy Stresses Legitimate Government for Rule of Law
item.description: Afghanistan's UN Chargé d’Affaires, Nasir Ahmad Faiq, stated that the rule of law requires a legitimate and accountable government. He criticized the Taliban's actions for enabling arbitrary power and human rights violations, emphasizing the need for women's equal rights and participation in justice. Faiq called for repealing discriminatory measures and supporting legal professionals.

item.title: WHO Urges Enhanced Mental Health Support in Afghanistan Amidst Daily Challenges
item.description: The World Health Organization calls for greater attention to mental health care in Afghanistan, noting widespread psychological distress due to loss and daily hardships. WHO representative Dr. Edwin Ceniza Salvador stressed mental health's parity with physical health, encouraging those in distress to seek support and emphasizing community solidarity.

item.title: Attempt to Illegally Export $44,500 in Cash Uncovered in Uzbekistan
item.description: Authorities in Andijan and Bukhara, Uzbekistan, have stopped attempts to illegally export a total of $44,500 in cash. In Andijan, $34,000 was found on a driver heading to Kyrgyzstan. At Bukhara airport, $10,500 exceeding the limit was found in a passenger's hand luggage.

item.title: Kazakhstan anticipates record sunflower harvest, farmers propose import ban
item.description: Kazakhstan expects a record sunflower harvest this year, with farmers expressing concerns about potential price drops due to cheap imports from Russia. Local farmers have proposed a ban on sunflower imports to protect domestic prices. The head of Aitas Agro noted that current prices are already low, with oil plants offering less than the cost of production.

item.title: Interpol chiefs from Central Asia meet in Astana to discuss regional security
item.description: Heads of Interpol bureaus from Central Asia convened in Astana for a meeting focused on combating transnational organized crime, international wanted lists, cyber threats, and financial crimes. The meeting included delegations from eight countries and aimed to strengthen coordination among law enforcement agencies in the region. Kazakhstan shared its experience in utilizing Interpol's capabilities.
